item.title: Michigan reports 2 deaths in rare parasite outbreak that has sickened more than 11,000
item.description: Two deaths linked to Michigan's cyclosporiasis outbreak had significant underlying health conditions impacted by the intestinal parasite and dehydration, health officials said.
item.content:encoded:
Two people in Michigan have died in connection with the state's sprawling cyclosporiasis outbreak, marking a rare fatal outcome from the intestinal parasite, health officials said Monday.

The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS) said the deaths were identified as part of the ongoing outbreak, which has so far sickened 11,234 people statewide. As of Thursday, 193 people with reported infections said they had been hospitalized.

According to the agency, medical records showed both people who died "had significant underlying health conditions that may have been impacted by cyclosporiasis and dehydration." Officials said no additional information about the cases will be released.

CYCLOSPORA OUTBREAK: IS IT STILL SAFE TO EAT AT RESTAURANTS? HERE'S WHAT TO KNOW

State health officials are continuing to investigate the source of the outbreak and said available evidence points to lettuce or salad greens as a potential culprit. However, investigators cautioned that other food items have not been ruled out, and no specific type of produce, grower or supplier has been identified.

MDHHS said it is working with local health departments and other partners as the investigation continues and will provide updates as more information becomes available.

WHITE HOUSE ADDRESSES GROWING PARASITE OUTBREAK AFTER MORE THAN 400 AMERICANS SICKENED

Cyclosporiasis is an intestinal illness caused by the parasite Cyclospora cayetanensis. The hallmark symptom of a cyclospora infection is watery, often "explosive" diarrhea that can last for weeks or even months if left untreated, the CDC says. Other symptoms include severe abdominal cramping, bloating, nausea, fatigue and significant weight loss.

Health officials emphasized that cyclosporiasis is generally not considered a life-threatening illness and that deaths associated with the infection are uncommon in the United States.

Fox News Digital's Angelica Stabile contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump DOJ corners school district with 7-day ultimatum over trans policy keeping parents in the dark
item.description: Harmeet Dhillon demands Anne Arundel County Public Schools stop hiding student gender identity information from parents or face DOJ litigation.
item.content:encoded:
Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon demanded in a letter sent July 29 that a school district in Maryland stop hiding information about student gender transitions from parents or face litigation from the Justice Department.

"By categorically withholding ‘(i)nformation about a student’s gender identity’ from parents except where ‘legally required,’ AACPS appears to have adopted a blanket, district-wide practice of nondisclosure untethered to FERPA’s enumerated exceptions … parents were denied access to their child’s full record, information was disclosed without parental consent, and the parents were denied a hearing to correct the record," she wrote, aimed at the Anne Arundel County school system. 

"Comply with the law or face us in court," Dhillon later added on X.

The demand marks the Trump administration’s latest effort to challenge school policies that allow students to socially transition without their parents’ knowledge, testing whether federal education privacy law requires districts to disclose gender-identity records. Anne Arundel County now faces possible litigation — and potentially the loss of federal funding — unless it reverses the policy within seven days, escalating a national dispute over parental rights, a significant plank in the president's policy agenda.

'SHAME ON YOU': SHERRILL KNEW VOTER-ROLL BOMBSHELL WAS COMING WHEN SHE CALLED TRUMP A LIAR, DOJ OFFICIAL SAYS

The Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) is designed to give parents the legal right to access their children’s educational records, which the Trump administration argues includes information related to changes in their gender identity. The law has previously been used by the DOJ in attempts to overturn similar policies in Maine and California.

LGBT advocates argue that nondisclosure for information linked to a child’s gender identity is important to preserving the safety of children growing up in non-affirming or abusive households. Social conservatives, meanwhile, take the position that schools don’t have the right to conceal information about their children from them.

Before Dhillon sent her letter Wednesday, the DOJ and the Department of Education announced that they had entered a partnership to crack down on transgender nondisclosure policies in both Anne Arundel County and Ann Arbor Public Schools in Michigan, potentially withholding federal funds from the district until it changes course.

VIRGINIA SCHOOL DISTRICT SUED OVER ALLEGED POLICY OF KEEPING STUDENTS' GENDER TRANSITIONS HIDDEN FROM PARENTS

In a press release announcing the joint effort, the agencies claimed that the Education Department had received complaints from parents in Anne Arundel County who alleged the district "was secretly helping their daughter pretend to be male at school" and declined to provide information about it when confronted.

An Education Department official told Fox News Digital that the agency does not comment on ongoing investigations and a DOJ spokesperson referred Fox News Digital to Dhillon's remarks when reached for comment.

Students enrolled in Anne Arundel Public Schools are, per district policy, allowed to use any name or pronoun they prefer, even if it doesn’t align with their sex, without requiring parental approval. Staff are, however, instructed to involve the student’s family in developing a support plan for the student unless "there is a genuine safety concern for the student’s physical, emotional, or mental health safety."

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION OPENS FOUR TITLE IX INVESTIGATIONS INTO MICHIGAN AND NORTH CAROLINA SCHOOL DISTRICTS

Additionally, the policy designates records about student gender identity as confidential medical information and advises that it should be revealed when legally necessary.

The Anne Arundel, Maryland, and Ann Arbor, Michigan, school districts did not respond to requests for comment when reached by Fox News Digital.

"School districts that hide information from parents are violating federal law," Dhillon said. "FERPA is not optional, and any districts that attempt to bypass or distort its requirements should expect immediate federal action. In partnership with the Department of Education, the Department of Justice will initiate enforcement proceedings with districts that fail to comply."

Dhillon's letter gives Anne Arundel Public Schools seven days to rescind its policy, provide parents impacted with the relevant records and inform staff that they cannot withhold information from parents. If the deadline is not met, the letter claims the district could face legal action.

item.title: Kamala Harris leaves Biden off list of top three 'most effective' presidents
item.description: Harris praised FDR's, JFK's and Barack Obama's legacy in her list of the most effective presidents, but notably left out the president she served under as vice president.
item.content:encoded:
Former Vice President Kamala Harris left former President Joe Biden off a list of her top three most effective U.S. presidents in an interview on Friday.

"In your view, rank the top three most effective presidents in American history," Marc Morial, the president of the National Urban League, asked Harris at the National Urban League conference on Friday.

She joked, "Marc, don't make me do that."

Harris then went on to name Franklin Delano Roosevelt (FDR) as her first pick and said she watched an NPR special about him recently.

KAMALA HARRIS IS THE 'FAIRLY OBVIOUS' 2028 PRESIDENTIAL FRONTRUNNER, DEMOCRATIC INSIDERS SAY

"It was he who talked about the expansion of the Supreme Court, and then he got ferocious back — kind of blowback for that. But he did good. It was Social Security. It was, you know, when I think about what he did in terms of investing in the people in during dire times and talking about the role and responsibility of government, that it should not just be about the benevolence of community organizations or just interpersonal relationships, that the government has a role. I think that he was a very important president," she said.

She went on to name John F. Kennedy — also noting Lyndon B. Johnson, Kennedy's vice president, who took over the presidency after he was assassinated.

"I credit, you know, Kennedy, of course, in terms of what he laid the groundwork for and then Johnson followed up on," she said. "Around having the ability, but that was again an example of the inside outside game. Because the reason that happened is because the pressure was on from the outside to appeal to the conscience of the people on the inside."

HILLARY CLINTON STILL FUMING OVER ELECTORAL COLLEGE, CALLS IT AN 'ABOMINATION' IN NEW NETFLIX SERIES

Harris listed Barack Obama as her third choice, which the audience applauded.

"What he did with the Affordable Care Act among many things, but in particular, if we had one issue that has been ailing America for generations, which is a healthcare system that has failed anyone other than the rich and addressing that the way that he did and took a lot of heat for it. I think it's one of the greatest presidents," Harris said.

The list notably left off Biden, under whom she served as vice president.

Neither Harris' office nor Biden's office immediately returned Fox News Digital's requests for comment.

Harris took Biden's spot at the top of the Democratic presidential ticket in 2024 after the former president decided to exit the race following a rough debate performance against now-President Donald Trump.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Harris had a little over 100 days to mount a presidential campaign, and wrote in her book after the election that his decision to run for a second term was reckless. 

"'It’s Joe and Jill’s decision.' We all said that, like a mantra, as if we’d all been hypnotized. Was it grace, or was it recklessness?" Harris wrote. "In retrospect, I think it was recklessness. The stakes were simply too high. This wasn’t a choice that should have been left to an individual’s ego, an individual’s ambition. It should have been more than a personal decision."

Harris took a series of left-wing policy positions during the conversation, and said she had not made a decision about 2028 yet.

"We must allow for a real conversation about revisiting certain things," Harris said. "I know this is gonna be controversial coming from me, in particular. We need to revisit the Electoral College."

Harris lost both the Electoral College and the popular vote to President Donald Trump in the 2024 election.

She also voiced support for expanding the Supreme Court.

"We need to revisit the point of expanding the court to 13 justices, like we have 13 district courts," Harris said. She also suggested the U.S. should revisit statehood for Puerto Rico, expanding beyond her previous support for statehood for Washington, D.C.

Zeteo founder and far-left commentator Mehdi Hasan reacted to a clip posted of Harris with a Biden animation where he appeared surprised.

The Independent's Eric Michael Garcia also reacted with a gif of the former president.

item.title: USMNT agree to new contract with coach Mauricio Pochettino through 2030 World Cup as obvious theme emerges
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino agreed to a new contract to manage the USMNT through the 2030 World Cup after leading the team to its first knockout win since 2002.
item.content:encoded:
Familiarity will be a theme for the U.S. men's national soccer team at the 2030 World Cup.

Despite major speculation before and throughout the 2026 World Cup that manager Mauricio Pochettino was leaning toward returning to the club level, the United States Soccer Federation announced Monday that the 54-year-old had agreed to a new contract to keep him on the red, white, and blue sideline through 2030.

"Working together with U.S. Soccer over the past two years, it has become clear to us that there is tremendous potential to make the Men’s National Team program even stronger," Pochettino said in the announcement.

LANDON DONOVAN SAYS SOCCER HAS ARRIVED IN AMERICA AFTER RECORD-BREAKING WORLD CUP SUMMER

"The passion we experienced from the fans throughout the World Cup only strengthened our belief in what is possible here. We are excited by the opportunity to bring all our experience and knowledge to even more areas of U.S. Soccer while helping strengthen the pathways for players, coaches and teams across the Federation. We want to try to have a lasting impact on the sport in the country that has welcomed us so warmly and for that impact to extend beyond results on the field."

Pochettino and staff led the USMNT to just its third World Cup group stage outright win in team history at the 2026 World Cup, as well as the squad's first knockout-stage win since 2002 with a 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina.

TAYLOR TWELLMAN GOES OFF ON TEAM USA AFTER DISASTROUS 4-1 LOSS TO BELGIUM: 'CAN'T MISS FUNDAMENTALS'

The USMNT was certainly looking to earn a spot in the quarterfinals, at minimum, in Pochettino's first run as World Cup manager, and while it fell short thanks to a wildly disappointing outing against Belgium in the Round of 16, it's difficult to say his re-upping with the national team is not a significant win for American soccer.

On paper, that is, at the very least.

For starters, it's hard to imagine the USMNT attracting a bigger, more-proven name than Pochettino to take over. On top of that, USA soccer presumably handing over more rein to a proven manager trying to build a team culture while the country continues to grow its own soccer culture feels like a no-brainer.

The 2030 World Cup will be jointly hosted by Portugal, Spain, and Morocco.

It is impossible to predict what the USMNT will look like in four years, but having the same manager building momentum who is already familiar with the territory, players, and prospects is a great first for the future of American soccer.

item.title: Softball hall of famer sends blunt warning to those defending inclusion of biological males in female sports
item.description: Hall of fame softball coach Leigh Ross-Dakich warns that allowing biological males in the WNBA will phase women out of their own league entirely.
item.content:encoded:
While the woke WNBA seems intent on speeding down a dangerous road toward biological males competing on its courts, pioneers in female athletics are sounding the alarm over where this could all end up.

During an appearance with her husband, Dan Dakich, host of OutKick show "Don't @ Me," Leigh Ross-Dakich, a hall of fame softball player who won over 500 games during head coaching stops at Bowling Green and Syracuse, issued a dire warning to those wokes like Golden State Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase who is on record seemingly defending the idea of biological males taking roster spots from biological females.

"Let's go. One league. Let's see what happens. What's going to happen is that girls are going to get wiped out," Ross-Dakich cautioned.

MARTINA NAVRATILOVA SAYS BILLIE JEAN KING’S TRANS-ATHLETE STANCE ‘DOESN’T SQUARE’ WITH HER OWN WORDS

And why would that be? Because there are physical differences between men and women. Obviously. But don't take our word for it, you should listen to gay rights hero Billie Jean King, who has said exactly that, only to then go on to advocate for including biological males in female sports.

Ross-Dakich, along with the likes of tennis legend Martina Navratilova, cannot understand why the likes of King and WNBA coaches are so married to their positions.

"The players that are here now, I don't know if they understand what women had to go through years ago in the '70s and '80s to get to a point where they actually could play and have their own leagues. I don't think they understand that," Ross-Dakich continued.

MEGAN RAPINOE SAYS EFFORTS TO BAR TRANS ATHLETES FROM WOMEN'S SPORTS ARE 'ATTACK ON WOMEN IN SOCIETY'

Billie Jean King no longer has a job to lose. The same goes for Megan Rapinoe. It's easy for them to earn political points with the Alphabet Mafia. But, at what cost to the future of female sports? Will they blink if a biological male decides to start identifying as female and takes a WNBA roster spot?

If these so-called leaders don't blink, Ross-Dakich believes the results will be catastrophic.

"If you want to do that and make one league, women will be phased out. These women that are fighting for women – women power – are now phasing themselves out of jobs," she added. "You're not saying that trans kids can't play. Whatever is on your birth certificate is where you should be playing. It's common sense."

item.title: Top Dem torches socialists taking over his party: 'They're anti-American'
item.description: Josh Gottheimer says Democratic Socialists of America are "not Democrats" and accuses them of trying to hijack the party as a vessel for socialism.
item.content:encoded:
A leading House Democrat went scorched-earth on insurgent socialists rising within his party, repeatedly telling them to start their own party and accusing them of trying to "hijack" the Democratic Party as a "vessel" for their communist, "anti-American," open-border platform.

House Intelligence Committee member Josh Gottheimer, D-N.J., a leader of the moderate Blue Dog Coalition, told Fox News on Sunday that the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) is "not Democrats" and rejected the idea that its platform is compatible with the Democratic Party’s.

"Obviously, I'm a very proud, commonsense Democrat, and I don't think DSA members are Democrats. They're socialists, right? And I'm all for them having their own party if they want one, but if they're trying to take over our party, that's unacceptable to me," Gottheimer said on "The Big Weekend Show."

DEM REP HENRY CUELLAR REJECTS DSA AGENDA, SAYS SOCIALISTS ARE TRYING TO 'USE' DEMOCRATIC PARTY

"Their values, their ideas are certainly not in line with ours, and they don't support our leadership. They're trying to use the Democratic Party as a vessel for their ideas. And as you heard in some of these conventions, literally, they're supporting the Communist Manifesto and [Leon] Trotsky, they're anti-American, they are anti-cop, they don't believe in borders."

Gottheimer was referring to man-on-the-street clips of DSA members at the group’s Chicago convention. One socialist said they are organizing a front to get "ICE off our campuses," while a member of the DSA’s National Political Committee said people such as Gottheimer who call them anti-American do not understand that their platform is the "most American thing you can do."

Another DSA NPC member said socialism is the "same kind of stuff that I am used to [in] growing up in the Christian Church."

DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS OF AMERICA ACTIVISTS SIGNED PLEDGE TO SUPPORT, DEFEND 'CHINESE SOCIALISM'

Gottheimer said 45 million voters are registered Democrats, compared with 150,000 official DSA members.

"They’re not welcome in the Democratic Party," he said.

He pushed back against members of his own party who have expressed openness to DSA-aligned candidates such as Maine oysterman Graham Platner.

GRAHAM PLATNER BLAMES NAZI TATTOO ON MILITARY ‘CULTURE,’ DRAWS BACKLASH FROM GOP VETERANS

Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., who represents Silicon Valley, said Democrats should not have "watched wealth pile up on Wall Street and Silicon Valley" at the expense of working-class Americans, adding that "the Democratic Party needs reform."

Gottheimer countered that fringe coalitions are mounting insurgencies in both parties and "trying to barge in" with incompatible ideas.

He also pointed to longtime Clinton confidant James Carville, who told Fox News that he would disown the Democratic Party if left-wing streamer Hasan Piker were permitted to become one of its leaders.

Former U.S. Marine Corps bomb technician Johnny Joey Jones asked whether Gottheimer would also leave the party over Piker or if Democratic leaders embraced socialists such as Harlem’s Darializa Chevalier.

"Well, [House Minority Leader Hakeem] Jeffries won’t — and let me be very clear that Hasan Piker is not a Democrat – the guy is the ultimate grifter, right? He’s the guy who said that 9/11 is America’s fault… We’ve got to make it clear he’s not welcome in the Democratic Party."

Gottheimer said the DSA platform shows that the organization is incompatible with the Democratic Party. He added that socialists can "scream and yell and try to …hijack [the party] and shove their ideas in and use it as a vessel."

"We have to make clear that’s not who we are…"

While Gottheimer reiterated that he does not plan to leave the Democratic Party any time soon, Jones noted that one prominent New Jersey Democrat already has.

Rep. Jeff Van Drew, whose district includes Cape May, switched parties during President Donald Trump’s first term, angering South Jersey Democratic committees as the longtime lawmaker embraced Trump’s platform.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"You wouldn't be the first New Jersey congressman to find a better party. I'm just saying leave the door open if you want to," Jones said.

Gottheimer’s district includes liberal New York City suburbs immediately west of the George Washington Bridge and the deep-red, Trump-friendly Skylands near the Delaware Water Gap, making it one of the most politically diverse districts in the state’s congressional delegation.

Fox News Digital reached out to the DSA and Piker for comment.

item.title: Iran reaffirms support for Hamas as Trump pushes to disarm terror group
item.description: Iran's president pledged continued support to Hamas' new leader even as Trump promotes his landmark Gaza disarmament deal and Board of Peace roadmap.
item.content:encoded:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian called Hamas’ newly elected leader to congratulate him and pledge Tehran’s continued support for the group’s cause, Hamas said Monday — as President Donald Trump promotes a landmark agreement intended to strip the terrorist organization of its weapons and power in Gaza.

Pezeshkian congratulated Khalil al-Hayya on his election as head of the group’s political bureau and told him Iran would continue supporting the Palestinian cause, according to a Hamas statement posted in Arabic, and reviewed by Fox News Digital.

"We are with you, and we support you in every action you take, despite the attacks we are facing," Pezeshkian said, according to Hamas’ account of the call.

Fox News Digital has asked Iran’s mission to the United Nations to confirm that the call took place and provide an official readout.

HAMAS TAPS 'ULTIMATE INSTITUTIONAL SURVIVOR' AS TERROR CHIEF, SENDING MESSAGE TO ISRAEL: EXPERT

The reported conversation highlighted a central contradiction confronting Trump’s Gaza initiative: While the White House is presenting the roadmap as a landmark agreement to remove Hamas from power and secure its weapons, Iran — the group’s longtime military and financial patron — was simultaneously reaffirming its support for Hamas and its new leader. Tehran’s backing raises fresh questions about whether Hamas is prepared to surrender the arsenal at the core of its power and how the Board of Peace could enforce disarmament against a group that continues to receive political support from one of Washington’s principal regional adversaries.

Trump in recent days announced what he called a "HISTORIC agreement for the COMPLETE DISARMAMENT of Hamas and all other armed groups," presenting it as a breakthrough after nearly three years of war. The stakes extend far beyond the wording of the deal: Hamas’ weapons remain the central obstacle to rebuilding Gaza, and the agreement will test whether Trump’s Board of Peace can enforce a postwar transition or whether Hamas will exploit the process to survive, regroup and retain power.

At the center of the effort is Trump’s Board of Peace, the president’s handpicked vehicle for implementing his Gaza policy and potentially extending his approach to other global conflicts. Trump chairs the board, whose executive leadership includes Secretary of State Marco Rubio, special envoy Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner and former British Prime Minister Tony Blair.

The White House says the board will oversee Gaza’s transition, mobilize reconstruction funding and hold the parties accountable.

But the tensions intensified Monday also on the Israeli side, when Nickolay Mladenov, Board of Peace director-general and high representative for Gaza, and board advisor Aryeh Lightstone met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and urged Israel to halt its attacks in Gaza.

Israel appeared to reject the board’s two central demands shortly afterward.

"Israel will not withdraw from its current line in the Gaza Strip and will continue to thwart any threat to our civilians and soldiers," an Israeli political official said. The statement amounted to a rejection, at least for now, of demands that Israel return to the "yellow line" and halt targeted strikes in Gaza.

A Board of Peace official declined to discuss the meeting but said the body remained focused on carrying out the roadmap.

"We are focused on implementation," the official told Fox News Digital. "We have provided a pragmatic path forward to transform Gaza by removing Hamas from power and seeing it hand over its weapons. These steps would undoubtedly allow for the improvement of life in Gaza and enhancement of security in Israel. We remain determined to advance these objectives."

Meanwhile, the Hamas terrorist group says it has agreed only to a phased and conditional process involving the storage of weapons after Israel stops its attacks, withdraws its forces and allows more aid into Gaza. Hamas has avoided the word "disarmament" in its statements and insists its weapons would remain under Palestinian control rather than being surrendered to Israel or an international force.

HAMAS AGREES TO COMPLETE DISARMAMENT UNDER 'HISTORIC' GAZA AGREEMENT: TRUMP

The board’s 15-point roadmap calls for Hamas to transfer Gaza’s civilian government and security responsibilities to a Palestinian technocratic body known as the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza. Hamas-run police would surrender their weapons to the committee, while heavy weapons, military production sites, weapons depots and tunnels would be addressed later through a phased decommissioning process linked to an Israeli withdrawal.

The intended endpoint is that only the new Palestinian authority would possess or control weapons in Gaza. But the roadmap leaves unresolved who will enforce the process, what constitutes compliance and which side must act first.

Hamas’ disarmament remains a central obstacle to rebuilding Gaza. Trump has tied reconstruction to the group laying down its weapons, while The Associated Press reported that the Board of Peace had secured approximately $7 billion in pledges by February — a fraction of the estimated $70 billion needed to rebuild the devastated territory.

Moumen al-Natour, a Palestinian lawyer from Gaza and co-founder of the anti-Hamas "We Want to Live" movement, said civilians desperately want the agreement to succeed but do not trust Hamas to relinquish power.

"Civilian people inside Gaza Strip… want safety, want to stop this war, want a new government, want to be alive," al-Natour told Fox News Digital.

But al-Natour, who previously was imprisoned by Hamas, warned that the group would use delays and violations to remain embedded in Gaza.

"I can’t trust Hamas because I know Hamas," he said, arguing that the group had repeatedly arrested and killed Palestinians who opposed its rule. He said an international force of only a few hundred personnel would be unable to secure Gaza or prevent Hamas from intimidating residents and that a much larger force and a new Palestinian police structure would be required.

Drawing on a grassroots network of thousands of Gazan professionals who reject Hamas’ ideology, the "We Want to Live" movement is promoting its own plan to rebuild Gaza’s civil society and is calling for cooperation with the Board of Peace and the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, the technocratic body tasked under the U.S.-backed transition plan with governing and rebuilding the enclave.

Al-Natour also proposed allowing civilians who want to escape Hamas-controlled areas to move into protected zones near the "yellow line" — the boundary separating Israeli-held territory from the rest of Gaza — where they could live under a new Palestinian administration backed by an international security force. He said the arrangement could provide Gazans with a safer alternative while a post-Hamas governing structure is established.

HAMAS SAYS IT WILL DISSOLVE GAZA GOVERNMENT, BUT ISRAEL WARNS GROUP STILL SEEKS HEZBOLLAH-STYLE CONTROL

Michael Milstein, a former military intelligence officer in Israel and now head of the Palestinian Studies Centre at Tel Aviv University, said the compromise has been developing for months under pressure from Qatar, Turkey and Egypt.

Milstein said Hamas may be prepared to give up control of Gaza’s day-to-day government and accept restrictions on heavy weapons but is unlikely to abandon its armed organization completely.

Under the model Hamas appears to favor, Milstein said, a technocratic government and international forces would assume responsibility for public services and reconstruction while Hamas preserves its personnel, infrastructure and political influence — an arrangement resembling Hezbollah’s longtime position in Lebanon.

"There is a very, very low chance that Hamas will completely disarm," Milstein told Fox News Digital, describing the roadmap as the kind of "gray area" Hamas has historically used to its advantage.

The Board of Peace also is pressing for an end to actions that could derail the plan. After Israeli strikes killed civilians and reportedly destroyed medical supplies over the weekend, Mladenov, the director-general of the Board of Peace, called for de-escalation but did not identify Israel by name.

"Two days of strikes across Gaza have killed civilians and destroyed medical supplies," Mladenov wrote on X, adding that he was working with the parties and regional mediators to "create the space for the full implementation of the President’s plan."

Israel, meanwhile, says it will not withdraw before Hamas genuinely disarms. Hamas says Israel must withdraw first.

The roadmap also faces resistance inside Israel’s government. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich and Settlements Minister Orit Strock urged Netanyahu on Monday to convene the security Cabinet immediately and block the international stabilization force from entering Gaza, according to Israel’s N12 news outlet.

In an urgent letter reported by N12 on Aug. 3, 2026, the ministers called the Board of Peace roadmap "dangerous to Israel" and argued that it contradicts Israel’s stated goals of disarming Hamas and demilitarizing Gaza. They objected that weapons would be placed under the authority of a new Palestinian body rather than removed from Gaza or handed to Israel and that Israeli troops would begin withdrawing while the disarmament process was still underway.

The far-right ministers also argued that the international force would monitor the separation between Israeli troops and the new Palestinian administration rather than directly disarm Hamas. They demanded that Netanyahu prevent implementation until the roadmap is revised to require full demilitarization before an Israeli withdrawal. The letter underscores that the plan’s obstacles extend beyond Hamas: Influential members of Netanyahu’s coalition are also challenging its sequencing, enforcement and security provisions.

That leaves Trump’s proclaimed milestone resting on the same question that has stalled previous Gaza negotiations: whether Hamas is truly preparing to surrender the weapons that underpin its power — or merely buying time to ensure that it remains standing when the rebuilding begins.

item.title: ‘Special sauce of crazy’ — Midwest Dem candidate’s policies too extreme for voters: opponent
item.description: Mike Rogers says he's ready to defeat either Abdul El-Sayed or Haley Stevens in Michigan's Senate showdown as the Democratic primary battle rages on.
item.content:encoded:
DETROIT, Michigan — Republican Mike Rogers is confident he'll defeat whichever Democratic rival he faces off with in the midterm elections in the crucial Senate showdown in this Great Lakes battleground state.

"It doesn't matter to us. We've looked at both candidates. We feel confident we're going to beat either one of those candidates that come out of that race," Rogers said in a Fox News Digital interview two days before Michigan's primary.

Abdul El-Sayed, a former Wayne County Health Department director who unsuccessfully ran an insurgent campaign for governor in 2018, is facing off for the Democratic Party's nomination in Michigan against Rep. Haley Stevens, a more moderate candidate backed by the establishment. The primary race is the biggest battle to date in the party's ideological war between the far-left and the center-left.

THE MIDTERM SENATE RACES THAT COULD FLIP THE BALANCE OF POWER IN CONGRESS

Rogers says both El-Sayed and Stevens "are very radical, and they are way too extreme for Michigan." And pointing to El-Sayed, he charged, "Abdul, he has his own special sauce of crazy."

The expensive and combustible scrum between El-Sayed and Stevens in the race to succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters, who is backing Stevens, is bolstering Republicans and potentially endangering a must-hold seat in November for the Democrats as they face an uphill challenge to win back the Senate majority.

"That certainly helps," Rogers said as he pointed to the Democratic primary battle.

Rogers, a former congressman who lost the 2024 Senate election in Michigan by a razor-thin margin while President Trump narrowly carried the state, touted that while the Democrats engage in what some describe as a civil war, "we've unified the Republican Party in a way I haven't seen in decades here on this particular race."

"We're building our team, our resources, and are ready for the fight after August 5 in a way I don't think Democrats are expecting," he highlighted.

El-Sayed, who, if elected, would make history as the nation's first Muslim senator, has made support for Medicare-for-all a major component of his campaign.

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

He has also called for abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and is a vocal critic of Israel amid its war with Hamas — even characterizing Israel's actions in Gaza as "genocide" against Palestinians. And El-Sayed, who served as a top surrogate on Sanders' 2020 presidential campaign, has vowed not to accept PAC donations.

El-Sayed, who is backed by many leaders on the left and was joined on the campaign trail two weeks ago by progressive champions Sen. Bernie Sanders of Vermont and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York, has reiterated that he's not a socialist.

But Rogers argued that El-Sayed is "in a different league altogether about pushing that socialist agenda, Democrat Socialists of America are in Michigan working for him right now. They're parachuting in from all over the country."

"If you believe in the future of America and your own prosperity and your individual liberties, well…. We're going to talk about it because they've got plans to take all that away," Rogers claimed, as he pointed to the far left and El-Sayed. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Both El-Sayed and Stevens are confident that Democrats will unite following Tuesday's primary.

"Let's make sure that anyone but Mike Rogers gets to the United States Senate," Stevens told reporters on Sunday. "After the primary, you're going to see a united Democratic Party. You are going to see us going full force, full fledge ahead."

And El-Sayed told Fox News Digital, "I think we all understand the risk of Donald Trump. We all understand the risk of Mike Rogers."

MEET THE FAR LEFT INSURGENTS WAGING WAR ON THE DEMOCRATIC PARTY IN THE 2026 MIDTERMS

"This is a guy who is not going to stand up and take on the war machine. He's not going to stand up and take on Big Pharma. He's not going to stand up and take on Big Tech. He is going to do the bidding of large corporations," El-Sayed argued as he referred to Rogers. "I think everybody understands what the stakes are. So I'm looking forward to welcoming everybody who might have voted differently in the primary."

Asked about El-Sayed's comments, Rogers charged, "The guy lies... this guy will lie from today until November 4, trying to get people to... walk past how bad he is for our state and our future in the country."

item.title: New York school pauses humanoid classroom robot pilot program
item.description: Salamanca City Central School District paid $57,590 for a Realbotix M-Series humanoid robot and AI program that was meant to launch in fall 2026 classrooms.
item.content:encoded:
A lifelike humanoid robot was expected to take a seat inside a New York high school classroom. Those plans are now on hold. The planned robot is reportedly stationary, with silicone skin and long brown hair.

Realbotix and Salamanca City Central School District had announced a limited pilot program for fall 2026 involving Optio, an artificial intelligence-powered  educational assistant, and one new Realbotix M-Series humanoid unit.

On July 24, the district announced that the pilot program had been paused while it works through enhanced student data privacy agreements with the New York State Education Department.

The district is also continuing discussions with community members and other stakeholders before moving forward. It has not announced a new date for the pilot program. The technology was intended to support AI and robotics lessons while teachers remained in control. Still, putting a humanlike machine in front of students raises questions about privacy and how quickly students may trust it.

CyberGuy Live: Missed "Sick of Spam?" Get the replay and checklist

Our free CyberGuy Live class, "Sick of Spam?", has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our spam-stopping checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you step by step through simple ways to reduce robocalls, spam texts, junk email and unwanted messages. You’ll also learn how to curb political texts, clean up your inbox and spot messages that could put your personal information at risk.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.

FOREIGN ROBOT BAN TARGETS CHINA OVER SECURITY FEARS

Salamanca City Central School District is located in western New York on Seneca Nation territory. The district had planned to introduce Optio to high school students enrolled in Woz ED AI and Robotics courses.

Realbotix previously described this as a limited fall 2026 pilot involving its digital assistant and one physical robot. The district has since placed the project on hold while it addresses student privacy agreements and gathers additional community input. Realbotix told CyberGuy, "The partnership also gives educators an opportunity to evaluate these technologies in a controlled classroom environment under district oversight."

The district reportedly paid $57,590 for the robot and AI program, according to the school board contract. Realbotix reportedly discounted the package from the M-Series robot's listed starting price of $95,000. The initial Optio rollout had been expected to expand to approximately 500 high school students during the fall semester. That planned expansion would have applied to the AI platform and student avatars rather than 500 physical robots.

The proposed project includes two connected parts. Optio is the digital AI educational assistant that students can access through personalized avatars. The M-Series robot would give that technology a physical presence in the classroom. Realbotix told CyberGuy, "Its technology combines conversational AI with a physical humanoid platform capable of natural interaction and lifelike expressions."

The company says its humanoid platform can use natural conversation and facial expressions during real-time interactions. The robot is designed to give students hands-on exposure to AI and robotics rather than limiting the lesson to a laptop screen.

The robot was expected to remain seated while using upper-body movements and facial expressions. The school reportedly requested a Western New York accent. However, Realbotix told CyberGuy, "The physical unit has not yet been deployed. Additional details regarding its implementation will be determined in coordination with the district."

That means some details reported about the robot may reflect the planned design rather than the finished classroom robot. The district had said the system would use school-approved curriculum instead of searching the open internet. When the technology lacked an answer, it was trained to say, "I don't know," rather than inventing information.

EDUCATORS WARN AI DEBATE HAS FOCUSED TOO MUCH ON CHEATING, NOT ENOUGH ON STUDENT LEARNING

Realbotix designed Optio as an AI educational assistant and an at-home tutor. Students will interact with avatars trained on district curriculum. The platform is designed to reinforce concepts and provide individual tutoring outside regular school hours. Realbotix says it can also offer homework support across multiple languages.

Students reportedly may be able to upload photos of homework for feedback. They could also request lessons based on their interests or receive real-time translations. Teachers may use Optio for lesson planning and curriculum adjustments. The physical robot could also provide prompts based on material already loaded into the system.

Realbotix told CyberGuy, "The program is intended to complement, not replace, teachers by giving students supervised access to emerging AI and robotics tools as part of the district's existing STEM curriculum." The company added, "Realbotix's products are designed to support human engagement and expand access to information and services while complementing the work of educators and other professionals."

The district has paused the pilot program while it works through enhanced student data privacy agreements with the New York State Education Department. It says appropriate privacy protections and community input are important parts of the process. The district has not said when those agreements could be completed or when the pilot might resume.

If the program moves forward, it would operate under district oversight with education-specific safeguards. Realbotix says those guardrails are designed to block inappropriate responses and reduce unreliable outputs. The robot and avatar would reportedly operate through a closed system without an open internet connection. The district also said Realbotix will lack access to personally identifiable student information.

The classroom robot would reportedly lack facial recognition and recording features found in some other Realbotix models. However, personalized learning requires the system to remember some information. Students will use unique identification codes when interacting with the technology. Those codes will allow Optio to retrieve learning information and continue earlier conversations without relying on a student's name.

Several media reports connected the school project to an adult-products business under the same parent company. Realbotix disputes the way some reports characterized that relationship.

Realbotix provided this clarification to CyberGuy:

"For clarity, some media reports have falsely connected the Salamanca project to an adult product or adult-products business. The Salamanca robot is a newly manufactured, purpose-built educational unit; no existing product or hardware is being modified or repurposed for the school." The company continued, "Realbotix LLC focuses exclusively on non-adult commercial applications, including healthcare and education. No adult-products company has any involvement in the Salamanca project or in any product or project developed by Realbotix LLC. Separate companies."

Realbotix Corp. describes itself as a holding company with two separately operated businesses. Realbotix LLC develops humanoid robots for commercial uses, while Intima LLC operates in the adult wellness and companionship market. The company says the subsidiaries maintain separate employees and facilities. It also says they do not share products, inventory, manufacturing resources or technology. Realbotix told CyberGuy, "The Salamanca robot is a newly manufactured, purpose-built educational unit; no existing product or hardware is being modified or repurposed for the school."

STUDY FINDS MORE AI PRAISE FOR BLACK STUDENTS, SOFTER TREATMENT OF FEMALES

Most students and teachers will not see a humanoid robot in the classroom anytime soon. Still, Salamanca's paused pilot shows where school technology may eventually be heading. Giving AI a face and a voice could make lessons more engaging. It could also lead students to trust the technology more quickly than they would trust a typical computer program.

Parents should pay close attention to what Optio remembers and who can access that information. Teacher oversight will also be important when the system gives an answer that sounds confident but may be wrong. A closed system would give the district more control than an open chatbot. Even so, students, teachers and parents deserve clear rules about student data and how the robot will be used.

The physical unit has yet to enter the school, and the district has not announced a new start date. Before moving forward, Salamanca says it will work through enhanced student data privacy agreements with the New York State Education Department and continue engaging with community members and other stakeholders. Many key questions will remain unanswered until those protections are finalized and students and teachers begin using the system in a real classroom.

Pausing the pilot program makes sense while the district works through student privacy agreements. The robot could make AI lessons more engaging, but families still need clear answers about what Optio remembers, who can access that data and when the district deletes it. The real test will come if the district restarts the pilot and shows that the technology can support learning without putting student privacy at risk.

Would you feel comfortable with a lifelike robot helping in your child's classroom, or does this take school technology too far? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

item.title: College football is finally back after months of NCAA lawsuits, NIL drama and congressional fights
item.description: After an offseason consumed by NCAA eligibility lawsuits and the Protect College Sports Act, fall camp signals football is finally back for the fans
item.content:encoded:
Lost in the kerfuffles over court cases involving the NCAA and the 'Protect College Sports Act' heading to the Senate floor this that week for a vote is the fact that we will play college football this month after another wild offseason of drama.

Can you feel it?

As football teams hit the practice field this week for the start of fall camp, the anticipation builds for what is to come in just 25 days after a majority of the headlines over the past seven months have centered around the future.

NCAA ROCKED BY COLORADO JUDGE'S 2022 CLASS ELIGIBILITY RULING THAT COULD RESHAPE COLLEGE SPORTS THIS YEAR

The expansion of the College Football Playoff. Congressional leaders trying to garner enough from SEC and Big Ten leaders to pass legislation that will have major ramifications on the future of college athletics. Court cases involving athletes who feel they were wronged by the NCAA installing a new 5-for-5 eligibility rule that gives athletes five years to play five seasons in all sports.

Bundle all of this together and we once again had an offseason that did not center around what was going to take place on the football field this year.

I am not implying that what is taking place off the field is not important, far from it. The NCAA put itself in this spot, and it's having to spend an insane amount of money to defend their decisions in courtrooms across the country.

What I am saying is that the average fan who just wants to cheer on their team, or call into their local postgame show to unload on whomever is coaching their favorite squad after a loss, is tired of hearing about the everyday noise that has overtaken the offseason.

And guess what? I don't blame them one bit. In reality, I agree with them.

We spent college football media days clamoring over the future of college athletics and how much money it's going to take in hopes of competing for a national championship. At the end of the day, fans that pay for tickets, parking, memorabilia, food, hotels and gas just want to sit in their seats to cheer on their team.

THREE INTRIGUING QUARTERBACK BATTLES TO WATCH DURING COLLEGE FOOTBALL OFFSEASON CAMPS

Whether that's inside the stadium or sitting on the couch with their friends, the conversation around what college sports will look like in two or three years has gotten old, quick.

Since the inception of NIL, which was highlighted by Nick Saban and Jimbo Fisher trading jabs about how much money was spent on the Texas A&M roster, the offseason talk has shifted from the on-field product to which lawyer is representing a player in their fight against the NCAA.

Again, that is just the world we live in now. It's not going away any time soon, no matter if Congress passes the 'Protect College Sports Act' or not.

All across the country, players and coaches are preparing for the upcoming season. At the same time, fans are booking hotel rooms or deciding how much money they will need to spend on streaming platforms so they can enjoy a season of college football.

Lawmakers praise bipartisan efforts led by Trump admin to ‘protect college sports for future generations’

We had plenty of drama though, thanks to figures like Brendan Sorsby, Lane Kiffin, the entire Texas Tech athletic department, Ole Miss and even Bill Belichick.

In Austin, there are Texas fans wondering if this is the year in which Steve Sarkisian can get the Longhorns playing for a national championship.

Out in Southern California, USC fans are already preparing to hold a picket line if Lincoln Riley cannot get the Trojans back into the CFP conversation.

The list goes on, and on. And, I love it. The local radio stations are getting everything together from a technical standpoint to host postgame shows that are like therapy sessions for fans.

We have also spent this offseason clamoring over who's the best conference in college football.

Is it the Big Ten or SEC? Well, who has won the past three national championships? Curt Cignetti rightfully stood at the podium last week in Chicago and made that point abundantly clear.

Will the ACC make another run at a College Football Playoff title game appearance, and can that team once again be Miami? Is this the final season in which Dabo Swinney will lead Clemson down the hill? How many vacancies will the ACC have after this season comes to an end?

There is a lot of pressure on schools to deliver, and if you aren’t in the CFP conversation when the first weekend of November rolls around, then fans will be prepared to start conversing about how much money was spent on a roster that came up short.

We have entered the most nerve-wracking point of the year in college football. The 'expectation' period, where everyone still has a chance.

This is what we crave. This is what we find ourselves stressing over when life might be kicking us outside the sports realm.

And sure, there will be plenty of noise around legislation and court cases that are currently ongoing off the field.

Unfortunately, that's the world we live in right now when it comes to college athletics. But, the beautiful sight of your favorite team running out of the locker room is nearly upon us.

Congratulations to you all. We've made it to another season of college football.

item.title: Virgin Mary statue becomes beacon of hope after California wildfires, Fox Nation explores
item.description: The Halpin family's Virgin Mary statue survived the 2025 Los Angeles wildfires, and their viral hymn around it became a powerful symbol of hope and resilience.
item.content:encoded:
The devastating 2025 Los Angeles wildfires reduced thousands of homes to rubble. But the survival of one family's Virgin Mary statue became a viral sensation, symbolizing the resilience of a community engulfed in flames.

Host Abby Hornacek uncovers the Halpin family's remarkable story in the brand-new, three-part Fox Nation series, 'Unexplained Mysteries of Faith.' In the final episode of the show, she visits Altadena to speak with Peter Halpin and his wife, Jackie, who recount the story of how their Virgin Mary statue survived destruction — and the viral hymn they sang around it.

"It was totally unintended," Halpin said. "As a matter of fact, we all just stood around. We said a family prayer that we say together, and then we decided to sing that song."

WORLD-FAMOUS CATHOLIC SHRINE TORCHED, 'DEVIL IN A SKIRT' SCRAWLED ON VIRGIN MARY STATUE

The Halpins reflected on how the comfort of their singing helped them through the initial shock of losing their house, and remarked that the statue's survival also impacted others.

"Being in that kind of state where you just lost your home and [are] in shock," he continued. "I think it gave a lot of people hope, because we believe in God, we are a prayerful family, and we just felt like it was something we should do."

During a January 2026 interview with Angelus News, Jackie echoed a similar sentiment, explaining how she couldn't recover from the emotional toll the wildfires caused without her faith. 

"I could not have done it without my faith," she said. "You can be really sad and still be grateful. You can be in pain and believe in redemptive suffering, and that has really sustained me this year. Offering all my sufferings back to Jesus — you just cling to the cross, and I just offer all my sufferings for my children and their needs."

WILLIE ROBERTSON'S FAITH-BASED ADVICE THAT'S KEPT HIS 34-YEAR MARRIAGE TO WIFE KORIE STRONG

Throughout "Unexplained Mysteries of Faith," Hornacek dives deep into sacred places, odd occurrences and personal stories that some say are shaped by miracles. 

In episode one, she travels to Loretto Chapel in New Mexico, which features a mysterious spiral staircase with no visible support, nails or a central column. 

Hornacek examines the bizarre disappearance of the carpenter who built it and how the unexplainable led to some citing faith as the reason behind its existence.

During episode two, she investigates the stunning story behind St. Frances Cabrini, the Italian-born nun who became America's first saint. Despite her chronic illnesses, she set sail to New York City to help Italian immigrants facing discrimination and opened 67 educational centers, orphanages and other public institutions during her lifetime. 

Her extraordinary strength is cited by her strongest believers as faith in action, with her legacy continuing across generations.

item.title: Dodgers send Wrobleski against Cubs' Boyd as both teams add arms before the trade deadline
item.description: Justin Wrobleski faces Matthew Boyd as the Los Angeles Dodgers and Chicago Cubs meet following their blockbuster MLB trade deadline acquisitions.
item.content:encoded:
The trade deadline is here. I am sure that excites a lot of people, including myself. We’ve already seen at least one massive trade, and we’ve seen a few others that have been interesting. There are definitely teams, like the White Sox, who are making a true push for the postseason with their moves. We knew the two teams in today’s game were going to be elite anyway, but both have made a move, and it will be interesting to see what else they do before the first pitch in this one.

The Los Angeles Dodgers made the move to get Tarik Skubal. Not only was he the best pitcher on the market, but he is the best pitcher potentially on the planet. Now a team that has won the past two World Series is more than primed for the third, and they will be getting to show him what it is like to be a Dodger before he hits free agency. Good for them. To be clear, the Dodgers are not bad for baseball. Cheap owners are bad for baseball. The Detroit Tigers organization is owned by people who have multiple billions of dollars in the bank, so they can’t cry poor.

Skubal won’t be starting today; that will come tomorrow. Instead, the team turns to Justin Wrobleski, who has been great this season with a 11-2 record, 2.88 ERA, and a 1.02 WHIP. These aren’t numbers he’s put up in a short period of time, either. He has tossed 112.2 innings this season. He did struggle in his most recent outing, going six innings and allowing five earned runs. Four of those came via the long ball, which really hasn’t been an issue for him this season. He faced the Cubs earlier this year, going six scoreless innings and allowing just four hits.

DODGERS REPORTEDLY ACQUIRE ACE TARIK SKUBAL FROM TIGERS IN TRADE THAT STIRS UP MLB WORLD

The Chicago Cubs are a Wild Card team, and that’s likely the best way to describe them overall. We know they are decent – their offense is among the best in the league. However, the team has been decimated by injuries. They had a thin pitching staff coming into the season and despite that being glaringly obvious to even casual followers, they didn’t do much to address it. The good news for Cubs fans is that they’ve fixed that issue a bit with some recent moves. They added Aaron Civale, and yesterday got a former Cy Young winner, Kevin Gausman.

He also won’t be making the start today, but it is a good addition to a team that is slowly getting some of their arms back. Matthew Boyd has returned to the rotation and has been a breath of fresh air for the Cubs. Since coming back, Boyd has gone 44 innings and allowed just nine earned runs. We got a really nice outing from him last start when he allowed no runs over seven innings and scattered just four hits. Dodgers hitters are batting just .200 against him in 100 at-bats.

This should be a really competitive game, and I think both pitchers are going to see that the opposition gets few opportunities. I think that the better option to take is the Cubs, but I’m not messing with the moneyline. I’m going to back the under 8.5 in this game. I just don’t see either starter giving up a ton of runs.

item.title: Fired ‘60 Minutes’ correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Scott Pelley wash up at Columbia Journalism School
item.description: Sharyn Alfonsi and Scott Pelley join Columbia Journalism School after clashing with CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss over "60 Minutes" changes.
item.content:encoded:
Recently fired "60 Minutes" correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Scott Pelley have found a safe space, landing at Columbia Journalism School (CJS) for the 2026–27 academic year.

Alfonsi and Pelley, who were shown the door from "60 Minutes" after clashing with CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss and objecting to attempts to tamp down the partisanship at the iconic newsmagazine, will serve at the historically liberal-yet-celebrated home to the Pulitzer Prize as journalists-in-residence, the school announced Monday.

Alfonsi and Pelley will "work closely with students, individually and as a group, through lectures, workshops and special events designed to sharpen their reporting, investigative and sourcing skills," according to CJS. They will also contribute to the Columbia Journalism Review. 

SCOTT PELLEY FIRED AT CBS NEWS AFTER BLOWUPS WITH BARI WEISS, NEW '60 MINUTES' PRODUCER

"This is a critical time for a free press," Pelley said in a statement. "Columbia is leading the way in training the next generation of great journalists, and I am honored to join Sharyn in that vital cause."

The Media Research Center believes "Columbia’s journalism program is not committed to honest journalism" and instead "delivers a one-sided education that celebrates left-wing policies and is overwhelmingly run by liberal journalists."

"The school uses its position as a leading journalism institution to promote a liberal agenda that has sweeping impact on the news Americans consume," the MRC said in a report on higher education. 

Meanwhile, Weiss has made several changes to "60 Minutes" during her tenure, which has been marked by sharp criticism from liberal media observers. Pelley was fired from the long-running CBS News show in June after he accused Weiss of "murdering" "60 Minutes" during a tense all-staff meeting that was supposed to be new executive producer Nick Bilton’s introduction to the staff. 

"She’s murdering ‘60 Minutes.’ She does not love this place. She was brought in to kill it and is doing exactly that," Pelley told staffers. 

SCOTT PELLEY HAS HEATED CONFRONTATION WITH NEW ‘60 MINUTES’ BOSS, ACCUSES BARI WEISS OF ‘MURDERING' SHOW

item.title: FIRST ON FOX: Trump to open direct line with military families in ground-up readiness push
item.description: Trump's executive order creates a Military Spouse Commission chaired by Jennifer Hegseth to address childcare, housing, employment and healthcare.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: President Donald Trump is expected to sign an executive order on Monday creating a new White House commission aimed at putting military families at the heart of military readiness, Fox News Digital has learned.

The executive order would establish the President's Military Spouse Commission, which would advise the president on policies affecting military spouses and families and provide annual recommendations to improve their quality of life while strengthening military readiness, a White House official told Fox News Digital.

The commission is designed to give the White House a direct line to the challenges facing military spouses, including childcare, employment, housing, healthcare, education and the demands of multiple deployments.

PENTAGON FIRES BACK AFTER MARK KELLY ACCUSES PETE HEGSETH OF TARGETING WOMEN AND BLACK MILITARY OFFICERS

Trump is expected to sign the order Monday afternoon alongside War Secretary Pete Hegseth, his wife Jennifer, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Dan Caine, and several military spouses, the official said.

The Military Spouse Commission will be chaired by Jennifer Hegseth.

"Military spouses are the bedrock of our Armed Forces' readiness and resilience. They are often overlooked but we see them and want them to know help is on the way," Jennifer Hegseth told Fox News Digital. "I am deeply honored to lead this Commission alongside my fellow military spouses in leadership. We will work tirelessly to dismantle the barriers our families face every single day and these families can rest assured they have a champion in the White House with  President Trump."

Trump will appoint an executive director, while Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin's wife, Christie Mullin, and 20 other military spouses representing the service secretaries, Joint Chiefs of Staff and each branch's senior enlisted leader will serve as commission members.

"The fight to support our service members is not just abroad, it’s also right here at home," said Mullin to Fox News Digital. 

TRUMP ADMIN'S PUSH TO SCRAP DEI IN FEDERAL GOVERNMENT TAKES LANDMARK STEP WITH NEW HIRING RULE

"My wife, Christie, has been supporting service members and their families in Oklahoma since before we entered public service and I can think of no better choice for someone to sit on this commission than her. In her role, she will continue leadership that demonstrates some of her greatest qualities: love, mentorship, and care driven decision making that will no doubt impact the spouses of service members in a positive way," Mullin added.

Military spouse employment and pay are the top concerns for active-duty military families, followed by time away from family, childcare, housing and housing allowances, and children's education, according to Blue Star Families' latest Military Family Lifestyle Survey.

An estimated 1 million children have at least one parent serving on active duty, according to government website Military One Source.

During his first term, Trump expanded support for military families by improving occupational license portability for military spouses, broadening access to remote and flexible work, and increasing opportunities for federal employment.

GOLD STAR WIDOW SAYS 'BLESSINGS ARE INFINITE' AFTER STRANGERS FLOOD HUSBAND'S ARLINGTON GRAVE

In 2018, Trump also signed legislation allowing military spouses to claim the same state of legal residence as their active-duty spouse, even when military orders require the family to move elsewhere.

In a Military Spouse Day proclamation signed in May, Trump said the nation's 250 years of freedom were made possible by the armed forces and the "selfless spouses" who have shared in the burden of military service across generations.

He acknowledged at the time "more work is needed" in relation to employment, quality housing, affordable childcare, accessible healthcare and education for military families.

"In times of peace and in the crucible of conflict, they rise to meet every challenge and bear the pressures and sacrifices with relentless grace and fortitude," the proclamation read.

item.title: Outrage over noncitizens allegedly voting in elections ignites probe into Garden State Dems
item.description: Jim Jordan and Bryan Steil demand documents from New Jersey on federal voting law compliance after 6,600 noncitizens were added to voter rolls.
item.content:encoded:
House Republicans are probing New Jersey's government after Gov. Mikie Sherrill admitted to more than 6,000 noncitizens being added to Garden State voter rolls in 2023 and 2024.

The GOP has been hammering New Jersey Democrats ever since Sherrill announced that 6,600 noncitizens were mistakenly added to the state's voter rolls during that two-year period, before she was in office, as election integrity sits as a key focal point ahead of the November midterms.

Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, and Committee on House Administration Chairman Bryan Steil, R-Wis., wrote to New Jersey Lt. Governor Dale Caldwell on Monday for more information on the state's compliance with federal laws surrounding elections.

HOUSE REPUBLICANS CONFRONT NJ GOVERNOR OVER 6,600 NONCITIZENS REGISTERED TO VOTE IN ALLEGED SOFTWARE FAILURE

"During a July 21, 2026, press conference, New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill announced that approximately 6,600 noncitizens were registered to vote between June 2023 and June 2024 because the state Motor Vehicle Commission (MVC) sent the information of noncitizens who accurately marked they were not citizens to the Department of State’s Division of Elections and the noncitizens were then registered to vote," Jordan and Steil wrote.

"According to Governor Sherrill, around 400 of these individuals successfully voted in elections since 2023. We write to express our serious concerns with New Jersey apparently adding thousands of noncitizens to its voter rolls and to request information from the New Jersey Department of State about its compliance with applicable federal voting laws."

Sherrill attributed the mistake to a "serious software error in New Jersey’s Motor Vehicle system."

GOP ERUPTS OVER 6,600 NONCITIZEN VOTERS FOUND IN BLUE STATE AS SCANDAL DEEPENS: ‘WORSE THAN ANYONE EXPECTED’

But it's unclear how many noncitizens have been able to register to vote beyond those two years, thanks to New Jersey motor voter laws that make it easy for people to go through that process during a visit to their local Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) location.

The revelations appear to undercut Democrats' assurances that noncitizens are not voting in U.S. elections, while feeding into Republicans' push for stricter federal standards at the ballot box. To date, however, there has been no evidence that shows noncitizens have swayed the outcome of any federal election.

"The vendor, IDEMIA, that provided the software that Governor Sherrill alleges caused the noncitizens to be registered refuted Governor Sherrill’s claims, stating that New Jersey agencies were to blame," the Republicans' letter said. "According to IDEMIA, the registration of noncitizens appears to have ended only when MVC asked IDEMIA to change certain settings in June 2024, but the noncitizens were not removed from the voter rolls and the issue was not publicly disclosed until now."

FEDERAL JUDGE BLOCKS DOJ ACCESS TO NJ VOTER ROLLS AMID STATEWIDE CONTROVERSY

"If the New Jersey government had access to accurate information about the citizenship status of the noncitizens who were registered to vote and were aware of the situation in June 2024, this raises additional questions about Governor Sherrill’s decision to blame IDEMIA, to not remove the noncitizens from the voter rolls, and to not disclose the issue to the public."

They pointed out that Caldwell, as the top elections official in the state, is "uniquely positioned" to help with House Republicans' investigation.

The committees are now seeking any and all information related to New Jersey's compliance with the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (HAVA), the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 (NVRA), and the Civil Rights Act of 1960 (CRA).

"HAVA governs the rules, maintenance, and technical coordination required for statewide voter registration databases. The NVRA mandates that state motor agencies serve as voter registration portals with requisite compliance protocols to maintain accurate and up-to-date voter rolls. The CRA requires states to maintain voter records and empowers the U.S. Department of Justice to vet voter rolls by cross-referencing lists to identify improper registrations," the letter said.

They're also looking for any documents pertaining to how New Jersey vets its voter rolls for eligibility as well as evidence of a "lack of cooperation" with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) in its aim to verify the citizenship status of each state's voters.

The letter is also signed by Rep. Jeff Van Drew, R-N.J., and Rep. Laurel Lee, R-Fla., both of whom chair relevant subcommittees on the matter.

They are requesting that New Jersey's government provide the documents by no later than August 17.

Fox News Digital reached out to Sherrill's office for comment.

item.title: Montana teen throws lasso to man in Yellowstone River in split-second rescue
item.description: A 14-year-old Montana rancher lassoed a drowning man from the Yellowstone River after a rafting accident, using cowboy skills he recently learned.
item.content:encoded:
A 14-year-old Montana rancher-in-training says God put him in the right place at the right time after he used the cowboy skills he'd spent months practicing to lasso and rescue a drowning man from the Yellowstone River following a rafting accident.

Jory Thomas was camping with his family near Greycliff, Montana, on July 5 when they heard someone screaming for help.

"We all heard, 'Help, help,'" Thomas told KTVQ. "There's two or three people floating down the river, one hanging on to the cooler, and he wasn't saying anything."

CALIFORNIA LIFEGUARD SPEAKS OUT ON HEARTSTOPPING OCEAN RESCUE: 'I LOVE WHAT I DO'

A raft and paddleboard had struck a bridge pillar, throwing four people into the river. Three reached shore, but one man continued drifting downstream while clinging to a cooler.

Thomas said there was no time to wait.

"This current was pretty fast then, and he was moving pretty quickly," he said. "Only thing I could focus on was helping him get out of the water because I didn't want to see anyone go in front of me."

He emptied his pockets, crossed a waist-deep side channel and ran along the bank. Then he grabbed a 12-foot lariat he'd brought from home — something his grandmother told the station he'd never packed for a camping trip before.

"My first instinct, I thought, was try and rope him and drag him out before he gets too far down the river," Thomas said. "Luckily, I caught him first try."

Thomas pulled the man toward shore through chest-deep water until first responders arrived.

OFF-DUTY ICE OFFICER RELIES ON 'SIXTH SENSE' TO SAVE DROWNING CHILD BEFORE DELIVERING MESSAGE TO CRITICS

The teenager said he'd only started taking roping seriously this year while helping with cattle on the family ranch, telling the station that his skills improving the more he roped cattle.

Thomas said he believes his faith guided him to act.

"God was basically putting me in the place of all this," he said. "God was just telling me all of this at the time and saying, 'Go get him, you got it, and I believe in you.'"

He later reflected that he never expected the same skills he learned on the ranch would save a person's life.

"I just thought I could help with cattle," Thomas said. "Not really helping humans and stuff like that. But I'm glad I was here to help."

The Sweet Grass County Sheriff's Office later honored Thomas with a Certificate of Achievement. Sheriff Alan Ronneberg and Undersheriff Ron Swanson recognized the teen for rescuing the man near Pelican Fishing Access.

"Well done, Jory!" the sheriff's office wrote in a social media post.
