item.title: Michael Thorbjornsen 'finally' arrives, Patrick Cantlay's gutless decision, and the FedEx Cup playoff bubble
item.description: Michael Thorbjornsen fired a bogey-free 63 to win the Rocket Classic, while Patrick Cantlay's puzzling strategy on a drivable par 4 raised eyebrows.
item.content:encoded:
Well, we're still waiting for that post-final major championship of the year hangover to set in.

A week after Jackson Koivun picked up his first win on the PGA Tour in just his third start as a professional, Michael Thorbjornsen earned his maiden victory on Tour at the Rocket Classic, making it back-to-back weeks that two of American golf's most highly anticipated players found the winner's circle.

While it has felt like a long time coming for Thorbjornsen to cross the finish line from an outsider's perspective, it's fair to say the wait has felt significantly longer for the 24-year-old himself after the journey he's already been on in his young career.

CHARLEY HULL PULLS OFF SAVAGE LOTTERY PRANK ON HER CADDIE AT WOMEN'S BRITISH OPEN

Speaking of a long time, it has been nearly four full years since Patrick Cantlay won a golf tournament, and based on his strategy during Sunday's final round at the Rocket, he seems perfectly content with that reality.

Finally, this weekend will mark the end of the PGA Tour regular season. As per usual, there are some big-time names on the outside looking in when it comes to punching tickets to the FedEx Cup Playoffs. We'll take a look at them and toss some predictions out there.

This is Par Talk, a weekly read to get you caught up on all the happenings that took place in professional golf that you need to know. You can follow Mark on X @itismarkharris and email him at mark.harris@outkick.com.

It's not entirely fair to pin the statement 'it's a matter of when, not if this player wins on the PGA Tour' on someone, because winning on the PGA Tour is outrageously difficult. Michael Thorbjornsen, however, has certainly had that sentiment attached to his name for years now.

It took Thorbjornsen 65 starts on Tour to earn his first victory, and while that number may seem somewhat large, context is supremely important to look at in the case of his career.

In August 2023, he suffered a stress fracture in his back that forced him to miss out on playing in the U.S. Amateur and a spot on the U.S. Walker Cup team. Later that same year, he underwent ankle surgery while still recovering from his back injury. He's also withdrawn from multiple PGA Tour events mid-round due to other injuries.

While overall he's hit the ground running since turning professional in June 2024 with 40 made cuts and 20 Top 25 finishes in his 64 previous starts before finding the winner's circle at the Rocket Classic, he's dealt with some battles most players in his age bracket avoid.

With all that in mind for the former Stanford standout, his come-from-behind win and slamming of the door on the 72nd hole made for a compelling scene on Sunday afternoon.

Thor began the day four shots off the lead, and while knowing he'd need his best stuff to climb to the top of the leaderboard, he went out and fired a bogey-free 63 to eventually snag a two-shot victory. It's worth mentioning he did so while playing alongside major champion Xander Schauffele, who was firmly in the mix on the back nine on Sunday as well.

Thorbjornsen has some catching up to do when it comes to fellow 24-year-old Tour players like four-time winner Tom Kim and three-time winner Akshay Bhatia, but it has been abundantly clear he has the tools, the speed, and a sneaky great game around the greens to jump into the upper echelons of players, not just younger players, on the PGA Tour.

Patrick Cantlay began Sunday's final round five shots back of the lead. Sure, that's a large deficit to try and erase, but firing a low round in the 60s and seeing what the leaders end up doing behind you seems like a game plan to implement when you're a guy searching for your first win since August 2022.

After getting to 2-under for the day through his opening five holes, Cantlay carded a bogey on the Par 4 7th hole, which is forgivable given it played as the hardest hole on the course on Sunday. He then sent a clear, embarrassing, and sad message on the eighth tee.

The Par 4 8th hole was the easiest hole on the golf course for the final round, playing at just 332 yards and drivable for a large chunk of the field. The overwhelming majority of players attempted to drive the green, and at worst, left themselves a chip shot of less than 20 or so yards, giving them a great opportunity at birdie, or maybe even an eagle.

Cantlay opted to hit an iron off the tee, leaving himself 130 yards to the pin. Mind you, Sunday's final round was played under lift-clean-and-place conditions given the rain the golf course had taken on overnight. The greens were incredibly receptive, and controlling spin with a full wedge shot as opposed to a chip shot makes the eighth hole significantly more difficult, but clearly, Cantlay didn't see it that way.

He ultimately hit his approach shot to 21 feet, missed the birdie putt, and walked away with a lifeless par.

Cantlay finished T-8, and of the 13 other players who finished T-8 or better, only Hideki Matsuyama and Michael Kim chose to lay up on the eighth as he did.

This week's Wyndham Championship is the final opportunity for players to earn a Top 70 spot in the FedEx Cup standings, earn a spot into the FedEx St. Jude Championship in Memphis, and keep their seasons alive, and there are some notable names who have to have big weeks in order to accomplish that.

Keegan Bradley (72), Jason Day (75), Brandt Snedeker (83), Brooks Koepka (86), Tony Finau (89), Lucas Glover (96), and Billy Horschel (107) will start the week on the outside looking in. That list of players has a combined eight major championships and two FedEx Cup titles between them. Despite winning just two weeks ago, Koivun is the bubble boy, beginning the week at No. 70 in the standings.

Of the names listed above, it's going to take each of the guys outside the Top 80 to have huge weeks to earn a spot in the field in Memphis. Snedeker's name stands out as a two-time Wyndham Championship winner. While Sneds has great history to lean on, Koepka has played the event just three times in his career, with the last being a missed cut in 2020.

Let's go out on a limb, however, and predict Koepka finally puts it all together this week, does enough and gets enough help as well, to sneak inside the Top 70.

item.title: 'The Exorcist' star Linda Blair speaks out after home searched in reported 100-dog kennel investigation
item.description: "The Exorcist" star Linda Blair says she and over 100 dogs are fine after Los Angeles County officials executed an inspection warrant on her rescue property in extreme heat.
item.content:encoded:
Linda Blair is speaking out after authorities searched her Southern California property as part of an active investigation into a reported kennel operation allegedly housing more than 100 dogs.

"The Exorcist" star, 67, said she and the animals in her care are "good" after a "surprise" visit from Los Angeles County officials on Friday.

Officials executed an inspection warrant as part of a joint operation between the Los Angeles County Department of Animal Care (DACC) and Control and the Los Angeles County Department of Regional Planning, according to People magazine. Officials told the outlet the operation was intended to evaluate the welfare of the animals and determine whether the property complies with county regulations.

"Checking in, I’m good. The animals are good in lieu of our surprise visit in 105° heat! With as busy as we all are in animal rescue and saving lives from the hot deserts and abandoned animals and shelters, everyone’s emails and social media are overloaded," Blair captioned a video posted to Instagram on July 31.

'EXORCIST' STAR LINDA BLAIR 'UNKNOWINGLY' WALKED AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD

"Turns out we just have some paperwork to do and some diagrams but as everybody knows, I’m looking to move so I can be more educational and help more animals. I’d rather move forward," she continued. "And I always say you know a good old-fashioned letter of contact always works. Be safe safe lives support animal rescue cause we’re all fighting to save lives.

The Oscar-nominated actress added that she has been planning to relocate her rescue operation.

The search was conducted after authorities sought to inspect a property "associated with a kennel operation reported to have more than 100 dogs," per People.

Officials alleged the kennel permits expired in 2023 and claimed multiple attempts to contact the property owner had gone unanswered.

"The warrant allows us to lawfully access the property and verify compliance with County codes," the department said in a statement to People, adding that investigators were assessing "animal care, safety conditions, and overall welfare of the dogs housed on the property."

"Our priority is the safety and well-being of both the animals on the property and the people who may be working or residing here," the statement continued. "This inspection will help us determine whether conditions meet required standards."

The DACC said the matter remains an active investigation and declined to provide additional details.

"As this is an active and ongoing investigation, DACC is not able to answer specific questions about this case at this time," the department said, adding that it is committed to ensuring kennel operations meet legal requirements and provide humane care.

TMZ, which first reported the search, said Blair was present during the inspection and cooperated with authorities. No dogs were removed from the property, according to the outlet.

In a video accompanying her Instagram post, Blair reiterated that the visit centered on administrative issues rather than the animals' condition.

"Today we got a really big surprise visit," she said in the video. "And as it turns out, there is nothing but some paperwork and some new diagrams and things."

"Wanted to check in and let you know I am fine. The animals are fine. And we just have some paperwork that has to be dealt with. And that's all this was all about. I don't know why mail isn't used more often to notify somebody. Just saying," she said, while also encouraging supporters to donate to the Linda Blair WorldHeart Foundation — the nonprofit she founded in 2003 to rescue and rehabilitate abused, neglected, and abandoned animals.

She ended her video by reiterating how she and the animals are doing, saying, "I wanna let you know I'm ok and so are the animals. Thank you so much."

Representatives for Blair and the Los Angeles County Department of Animal Care and Control did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: 49ers betting preview suggests Rams and Seahawks could overtake San Francisco for playoffs

Technology is fun. I wrote this article once already, and something happened where it disappeared altogether. I really don’t know what the issue is or was, but maybe the second time I dissect the San Francisco 49ers' upcoming season will be even more exciting than the first time.

This was a team that I struggled to bet on or against last season. When I was betting they would lose, they came out with some miracle game. When I bet they would win, they looked like they had never played football before. I can still admit that the squad was impressive despite navigating a wide range of injuries. They were 12-5 for the season and got a 5-3 record from their backup quarterback, Mac Jones. Every loss they took in the regular season was against a postseason team, with the exception of Tampa Bay. They did win the first game of the postseason, taking out the reigning Super Bowl champion Eagles. Then disaster struck against the Seahawks. They gave up a game-opening kickoff return for a touchdown. Then turned the ball over on downs, leading to a Seattle field goal. A fumble and another Seattle touchdown put them down 17-0 after the first quarter. The second half was even worse in many ways. They turned the ball over on downs, then had an interception, turnover on downs, fumble, punt, and then ran three meaningless plays to end the game.

49ERS BRING BACK DEEBO SAMUEL TO FILL VOID LEFT BY RICKY PEARSALL'S KNEE INJURY: REPORT

The team that deals with many injuries at many positions took a shot with someone uber talented, but also coming off of an injury-marred season.
